fatal_errors: The target intervention is approximately 10 at.% Al in an AlTiCrZrNbTa refractory high-entropy-alloy coating, not 10 at.% Al added to an elemental Cr coating.
The proposed interfacial Al-rich oxide barrier is inconsistent with the target mechanism, in which a surface Al2O3-TiO2-Cr2O3 composite scale suppresses inward oxygen transport.
The hypothesis attributes failure and protection primarily to Cr-Zr interdiffusion, whereas the target evidence concerns steam oxidation, oxygen penetration, oxide continuity, and coating adhesion.
The proposed 1100-1200 degrees Celsius exposures lasting several hours substantially exceed the demonstrated boundaries of 1000 degrees Celsius for 60 minutes and 1100 degrees Celsius for 30 minutes.
The cited evidence does not establish that a binary Cr-10 at.% Al coating forms the claimed interfacial barrier or suppresses Cr-Zr interdiffusion on zirconium alloy.
explanation: The response captures one target-associated motif—an optimum near 10 at.% Al—and provides a reasonably discriminating comparison against pure Cr using interdiffusion profiling, oxide characterization, adhesion testing, and autoclave corrosion. However, it reconstructs a materially different system. The hidden study varied Al in a six-component AlTiCrZrNbTa coating and found protection through a dense surface composite oxide; it did not demonstrate a binary Cr-Al coating or an Al-rich oxide at the coating-substrate interface. It also misses the nonmonotonic composition dependence, including failure at 17-25 at.% Al due to intermetallic formation and oxide discontinuity. Conditions and outcomes are overstated: normal-PWR preservation and multi-hour performance at 1100-1200 degrees Celsius were not established. E2 supports an intermediate-Al optimum only in a different AlNbTiZr coating and oxide chemistry, while E1 is a remote Cu-Si diffusion-barrier analogy. Thus the hypothesis is testable and somewhat plausible, but its central intervention and mechanism lack direct supporting evidence and do not reconstruct the target.
